arxiv-2108-01867.title: A Pragmatic Look at Deep Imitation Learning
arxiv-2108-01867.creator: Kai Arulkumaran, Dan Ogawa Lillrank
arxiv-2108-01867.description: Abstract The introduction of the generative adversarial imitation learning (GAIL) algorithm has spurred the development of scalable imitation learning approaches using deep neural networks. Many of the algorithms that followed used a similar procedure, combining on-policy actor-critic algorithms with inverse reinforcement learning. More recently there have been an even larger breadth of approaches, most of which use off-policy algorithms.

arxiv-2201-04552.title: Generating enhanced primordial GWs during inflation with intermittent violation of NEC and diminishment of GW propagating speed
arxiv-2201-04552.creator: Yun-Song Piao
arxiv-2201-04552.description: Abstract We investigate both the null energy condition (NEC) violating scenario and the c T c_{T} -diminishing scenario for generating enhanced power spectrum of primordial gravitational waves (GWs) during inflation, where c T c_{T} is the propagating speed of primordial GWs.

arxiv-2202-01909.title: ad-datasets: a meta-collection of data sets for autonomous driving
arxiv-2202-01909.creator: Daniel Bogdoll, Felix Schreyer, and J. Marius Zöllner FZI Research Center for Information Technology, Germany Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, Germany bogdoll@fzi.de
arxiv-2202-01909.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Daniel Bogdoll, Felix Schreyer, and J. Marius Zöllner FZI Research Center for Information Technology, Germany Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, Germany bogdoll@fzi.de. Autonomous driving is among the largest domains in which deep learning has been fundamental for progress within the last years. The rise of datasets went hand in hand with this development.

arxiv-2211-03565.title: A dataset of direct observations of sea ice drift and waves in ice
arxiv-2211-03565.creator: Jean Rabault, Malte Müller, Joey Voermans, Dmitry Brazhnikov, Ian Turnbull, Aleksey Marchenko, Martin Biuw, Takehiko Nose, Takuji Waseda, Malin Johansson, Øyvind Breivik, Graig Sutherland, Lars Robert Hole, Mark Johnson, Atle Jensen, Olav Gundersen, Yngve Kristoffersen, Alexander Babanin, Paulina Te
arxiv-2211-03565.description: Abstract Variability in sea ice conditions, combined with strong couplings to the atmosphere and the ocean, lead to a broad range of complex sea ice dynamics. More in-situ measurements are needed to better identify the phenomena and mechanisms that govern sea ice growth, drift, and breakup.

arxiv-2412-00033.title: Can an AI Agent Safely Run a Government? Existence of Probably Approximately Aligned Policies
arxiv-2412-00033.creator: Frédéric Berdoz, Roger Wattenhofer
arxiv-2412-00033.description: Abstract While autonomous agents often surpass humans in their ability to handle vast and complex data, their potential misalignment (i.e., lack of transparency regarding their true objective) has thus far hindered their use in critical applications such as social decision processes. More importantly, existing alignment methods provide no formal guarantees on the safety of such models.

arxiv-2412-13983.title: GraphAvatar: Compact Head Avatars with GNN-Generated 3D Gaussians
arxiv-2412-13983.creator: Xiaobao Wei, Peng Chen, Ming Lu, Hui Chen, Feng Tian
arxiv-2412-13983.description: Abstract Rendering photorealistic head avatars from arbitrary viewpoints is crucial for various applications like virtual reality. Although previous methods based on Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) can achieve impressive results, they lack fidelity and efficiency. Recent methods using 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) have improved rendering quality and real-time performance but still require significant storage overhead.

arxiv-2508-01931.title: Marlin : Efficient Coordination for Autoscaling Cloud DBMS (Extended Version) Price: 15.00 ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06
arxiv-2508-01931.creator: Wenjie Hu, Guanzhou Hu, Mahesh Balakrishnan, Xiangyao Yu
arxiv-2508-01931.description: Abstract . Modern cloud databases are shifting from converged architectures to storage disaggregation, enabling independent scaling and billing of compute and storage. However, cloud databases still rely on external, converged coordination services (e.g., ZooKeeper) for their control planes. These services are effectively lightweight databases optimized for low-volume metadata.

arxiv-2509-23783.title: Falcon: A Cross-Modal Evaluation Dataset for Comprehensive Safety Perception Thanks: ♠ \spadesuit These authors contributed equally to this work. Thanks: † \dagger Corresponding author.
arxiv-2509-23783.creator: Qi Xue ♠ \spadesuit, Minrui Jiang ♠ \spadesuit, Runjia Zhang ♠ \spadesuit, Xiurui Xie † \dagger, Pei Ke, Guisong Liu
arxiv-2509-23783.description: Abstract Existing methods for evaluating the harmfulness of content generated by large language models (LLMs) have been well studied. However, approaches tailored to multimodal large language models (MLLMs) remain underdeveloped and lack depth. This work highlights the crucial role of visual information in moderating content in visual question answering (VQA), a dimension often overlooked in current research.

arxiv-2602-03132.title: Contrastive Concept-Tree Search for LLM-Assisted Algorithm Discovery
arxiv-2602-03132.creator: Timothee Leleu, Sudeera Gunathilaka, Federico Ghimenti, Surya Ganguli
arxiv-2602-03132.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Timothee Leleu, Sudeera Gunathilaka, Federico Ghimenti, Surya Ganguli. Large language Model (LLM)-assisted algorithm discovery is an iterative, black-box optimization process over programs to approximatively solve a target task, where an LLM proposes candidate programs and an external evaluator provides task feedback. Despite intense recent research on the topic and promising results, how can the LLM internal representation of the space of possible programs be maximally exploited to improve performance is an open question.

pmc-10656657.title: Public Perceptions About Monkeypox on Twitter: Thematic Analysis
pmc-10656657.creator: Abimbola Leslie, Omolola Okunromade, Abeed Sarker
pmc-10656657.description: BackgroundSocial media has emerged as an important source of information generated by large segments of the population, which can be particularly valuable during infectious disease outbreaks. The recent outbreak of monkeypox led to an increase in discussions about the topic on social media, thus presenting the opportunity to conduct studies based on the generated data.

pmc-10802108.title: Characterization of long-term ex vivo expansion of tree shrew spermatogonial stem cells
pmc-10802108.creator: Cong Li, Rui Bi, Lin Wang, Yu-Hua Ma, Yong-Gang Yao, Ping Zheng
pmc-10802108.description: Tree shrews (Tupaia belangeri chinensis) share a close relationship to primates and have been widely used in biomedical research. We previously established a spermatogonial stem cell (SSC)-based gene editing platform to generate transgenic tree shrews. However, the influences of long-term expansion on tree shrew SSC spermatogenesis potential remain unclear.

pmc-11653707.title: Expression of mTOR, CD163, α-SMA, FOXp3 as survival predictors and its significance in patients with oral squamous cell carcinoma
pmc-11653707.creator: Suganya Ramalingam, Sivaramakrishnan Shantha, Chakravarthy Purushothaman Srinivasan, Nagarajan Priyathersini, Susruthan Muralitharan, Uma Sudhakar, Harikrishnan Thamizhchelvan, Venkatachalam Deepa Parvathi
pmc-11653707.description: BackgroundOral cancer; categorised under head and neck cancers (HNC) predominantly originates from squamous cells and is referred as oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). Various factors (internal and external) causes OSCC. PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathways are known to be primarily mutated in HNC. mTOR remains as a key regulator for various physiological and developmental processes in normal and cancer cells.

pmc-13073859.title: Microarray-Based Genomic Profiling in Low-Dose Radiation Research: Evidence, Limitations, and Translational Perspectives
pmc-13073859.creator: Sandugash Auganbayeva, Meruyert Massabayeva, Nailya Chaizhunussova, Dariya Shabdarbayeva, Lyudmila Pivina, Andrey Orekhov, Zhanargul Smailova, Saulesh Apbassova, Vladlena Sabitova, Tokzhan Akhmadiyeva, Saule Kozhanova, Dinara Mukanova, Murat Lepesbayev, Assel Baibussinova, Alexandra Lipikhina, Yulia
pmc-13073859.description: Low-dose ionizing radiation exposure remains a major challenge for long-term health risk assessment, particularly in retrospective cohorts with heterogeneous exposure scenarios and limited biological material. Although next-generation sequencing (NGS) technologies dominate contemporary molecular research, DNA microarrays remain relevant in radiation biology due to their standardization, reproducibility, cost-effectiveness, and compatibility with archived biospecimens.

pmc-13194727.title: First-principles study of phenol sensing properties on β-arsenic phosphide monolayers
pmc-13194727.creator: M. Vijay Balaji, R. Chandiramouli, R. Bhuvaneswari, V. Nagarajan
pmc-13194727.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). For the very first time, we investigate the adsorption properties of β-arsenic phosphide (β-AsP) monolayer towards the phenolic compounds using first-principles calculations. Firstly, the structural and electronic features of the β-AsP monolayer are studied. The band structure, projected density of states, charge transfer, adsorption energy, recovery time, and work function are estimated for the different phenolic compounds, such as phenol, methyl phenol, dimethyl phenol, chlorophenol, and nitrophenol, adsorbed on the β-AsP monolayer. All the compounds are physisorbed on the β-AsP monolayer surface.

pmc-13289005.title: Developing general practitioner and consumer supports for genomics in Australian primary care: a mixed-methods protocol
pmc-13289005.creator: Janet C Long, Alison D Archibald, Klay Lamprell, Belinda Dawson-McClaren, Claudine Kraan, Amanda Springer, Lisa Dive, Ainsley J Newson, Gabriel Watts, Isabella Holmes, Henry Cutler, Varinder Jeet, Alison Trainer, Stephanie Best, Martin Delatycki, Edwin P Kirk, Nigel Laing, Monica Ferrie, Lucinda Freeman, Simon Willcock, Samantha Spanos, Lucy Gilkes, Julie Cini, Samantha Edwards, Ruth Leibowitz, Janani Mahadeva, Darran Foo, Kate Churruca, Romika Patel, Jeffrey Braithwaite

pmc-13371360.title: Frequency-domain band-pass filtering enhanced pulsation method for pulmonary embolism diagnosis and risk stratification: a two-center retrospective study
pmc-13371360.creator: Shaofei Xu, Jiazheng Li, Ziqi Li, Yuxuan Cai, Junlai Zhao, Rongrong Zhu, Maokun Li, Weiwei Wu
pmc-13371360.description: BackgroundPulmonary embolism (PE) remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality in critical care, yet traditional diagnostic methods face limitations, especially in critically ill patients. This study introduces a novel frequency-domain band-pass filtering enhanced electrical impedance tomography (EIT) pulsation method for rapid, non-invasive PE diagnosis and risk stratification.

pmc-13413978.title: The Environmental Occurrence of Pharmaceutical Residues, Agrochemical Contaminants, and Antimicrobial Resistance in a Wastewater-Impacted Urban Water System: A One Health Assessment
pmc-13413978.creator: Amos Misi, Paul Mushonga, Thelma Mari, Greathyl T. Zinyengere, Trinity Njenje, Mary Chipo Mhungu, Pamhidzai Dzomba, Rudo Zhou, Mark F. Zaranyika
pmc-13413978.description: Urban water security in many cities in the Global South is increasingly challenged by ageing infrastructure and the presence of persistent chemical contaminants. This study investigated the Harare metropolitan water continuum between 2020 and 2024 using a longitudinal, systems-oriented observational framework encompassing wastewater discharge, surface water reservoirs, drinking water treatment, and municipal distribution networks.

pmc-13450438.title: The PIRAGUA_atmos_analysis and PIRAGUA_hydro_analysis: Water balance components data sets for the Pyrenees
pmc-13450438.creator: Leticia Palazón, Pere Quintana-Seguí, Roger Clavera-Gispert, Anaïs Barella-Ortiz, Youen Grusson, Roxelane Cakir, Sabine Sauvage, José Miguel Sánchez-Pérez, Santiago Beguería
pmc-13450438.description: The PIRAGUA_atmos_analysis and PIRAGUA_hydro_analysis datasets have been developed to support a comprehensive assessment of current water resources across the Pyrenees region, encompassing Spain, France, and Andorra. PIRAGUA_atmos_analysis is a daily, gridded dataset of near-surface meteorological variables designed to serve as input for hydrological and land-surface models.

pmc-13495200.title: Preoperative and perioperative predictors of prolonged hospital stay after uncomplicated elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-13495200.creator: Ramazan Topcu, Turker Kaymak, Mahmut Arif Yüksek, Orhan Aslan, Elif Yiğit Kaymak, İsmail Sezikli, Kaan Canal, Aşkın Kadir Perçem

pmc-13530530.title: Poster 225. Latarjet Offers Lower Two-Year Re-operation Rate with Similar Rate of Nerve Injury Compared to Anterior Free Bone Block Procedures
pmc-13530530.creator: Natalie K. Kucirek, Marcus V. Trotter, Brian T. Feeley, Benjamin Ma, Alan L. Zhang, Drew A. Lansdown
pmc-13530530.description: Objective:The objective of this study is to determine rates of re-operation and associated risk factors after complex shoulder stabilization surgery, with a focus on comparing the Latarjet procedure to anterior free bone block procedures. Rates of nerve injury after these procedures will be determined. Additionally, national utilization trends in complex shoulder stabilization surgery will be identified.

pmc-13545567.title: Contrast-enhanced ultrasound-guided precision fibrinolysis for refractory loculated chylothorax after lung transplantation: a case report
pmc-13545567.creator: Tingting Jiang, Wuxi Chen, Zifeng Peng, Shuyi Qiu, Guosheng Liang, Qing Tang, Liantu He

pmc-13616665.title: Dynamic representation of music induced emotion regulation and neuroendocrine responses
pmc-13616665.creator: Shuang Shi
pmc-13616665.description: IntroductionThis study introduces a novel methodology for dynamically representing the regulation of music-induced emotions and associated neuroendocrine responses. The research addresses the limitations of traditional approaches, which often fail to capture the intricate and dynamic interactions between musical stimuli and the resulting emotional and physiological changes.
